# Routing-socket messages captured on a Mac (macOS 27.2, kern.osversion 26B131, Wi-Fi en0 behind a
# home router; four system utun interfaces with interface-scoped IPv6 default routes) by an
# unprivileged C program: `RTM_GET` replies (`write` an rt_msghdr + RTA_DST + an empty RTA_IFP
# sockaddr_dl to a PF_ROUTE socket, `read` the reply with our rtm_pid/rtm_seq), and one
# `sysctl {CTL_NET, PF_ROUTE, 0, 0, NET_RT_DUMP, 0}` buffer. Bytes are as the kernel wrote them,
# except: the ISP's IPv6 prefix 2606:a300:9024:184::/64 is rewritten to 2001:db8:9024:184::/64 and
# the router's EUI-64 link-local interface id to ::fe00:1 (same lengths; KAME embedded scope ids
# kept). Link-layer addresses come masked by the kernel (02:00:00:00:00:00) for unprivileged readers.
# Format: `get <destination> <hex reply>` or `dump <hex>`.
get 8.8.4.4 
get 1.1.1.1 
get 192.168.1.1 
get 192.168.1.50 
get 192.168.1.213 
get 127.0.0.1 
get 2606:4700:4700::1111 
get ::1 
get 2001:db8:9024:184:2cd3:b59f:bfaa:3b77 
get 2001:db8:9024:184::99 
get fe80::1 
dump
